# Satwik Ghanta

I am a PhD candidate in **Computing Science** at the **University of Glasgow**, working on **Sustainable Software Engineering**, **Responsible AI for Software Engineering**, and **Human-Computer Interaction for Software Engineering**.

My research explores how software teams understand, reason about, and integrate sustainability into development practice, with particular attention to the human, organisational, and technical dimensions of software engineering.

[Email me](mailto:y.ghanta.1@research.gla.ac.uk){.btn .btn-primary} [View publications](publications.qmd){.btn .btn-secondary}
:::

## Research focus

My research focuses on sustainability in software engineering teams and organisations. I study how sustainability is interpreted in real-world software development settings, how it becomes part of everyday practice, and what challenges teams face when trying to make software engineering more sustainable.

I am especially interested in empirical software engineering, sustainability-aware software practices, responsible AI, and the role of human values in technical decision making. My work connects software engineering with organisational practice, stakeholder participation, and the design of tools and processes that support more socially responsible technology development.

## Recent updates

- **March 2026:** Our paper **"Practical Feasibility of Sustainable Software Engineering Tools and Techniques"** was accepted to the **FSE 2026 Industry Papers** track.
- **January 2026:** Our preprint **"Empowering Affected Individuals to Shape AI Fairness Assessments: Processes, Criteria, and Tools"** became available.
- **2025:** Our paper **"Perspectives, Needs and Challenges for Sustainable Software Engineering Teams: A FinServ Case Study"** was published at **ESEM 2025**.

## Selected work

::: {.grid}
::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-4}
### Sustainable Software Engineering Teams

I study how software practitioners and organisations understand sustainability, what challenges they face, and how sustainability can be meaningfully integrated into software engineering practice.
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-4}
### Sustainable Software Tools and Techniques

My work examines the practical feasibility of sustainable software engineering tools in real-world industrial contexts, including how practitioners evaluate tools based on workflow fit, data requirements, interpretability, and organisational constraints.
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-4}
### Responsible and Participatory AI

I am interested in how people affected by AI systems can participate in shaping fairness assessments, especially in high-stakes contexts where fairness, values, and lived experiences matter.
:::
:::

## Background

Alongside my PhD, I have experience as a software engineer working on web-based applications and software projects. This practical background informs my research interest in software teams, developer practices, sustainable coding, security, and the organisational realities that shape software engineering work.
